title: Psychiatric Disorders: How They Are Classified
source: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine, Medical Psychiatry, Box 31.1 (WHO ICD-10, Chapter V F00-F99) and Box 31.2

beats.vo: Every psychiatric diagnosis lives in one chapter of ICD-10. And it has just ten blocks.
Here they are, straight from Davidson's table.

beats.name: Organic
beats.vo: One. Organic mental disorders. Dementia, delirium, and disorders due to brain damage or disease.

beats.name: Psychoactive substances
beats.vo: Two. Psychoactive substances: alcohol, opioids, cannabinoids. Intoxication, harmful use, dependence and withdrawal.

beats.name: Mood
beats.vo: Four. Mood, or affective, disorders. Depression and bipolar disorder.

beats.name: Neurotic & stress-related
beats.vo: Five. Neurotic, stress-related and somatoform disorders. Phobias, generalised anxiety, OCD, PTSD and adjustment disorders.

beats.name: Physiological disturbance
beats.vo: Six. Behavioural syndromes with physiological disturbance. Anorexia, bulimia and sexual dysfunction.

beats.name: Adult personality
beats.vo: Seven. Disorders of adult personality and behaviour. Specific personality disorders, trichotillomania and gender identity disorders.

beats.name: Mental retardation
beats.vo: Eight. Mental retardation, now called intellectual disability. Mild, moderate, severe or profound.

beats.name: Psychological development
beats.vo: Nine. Disorders of psychological development. Autism and Asperger syndrome.

beats.name: Childhood
beats.vo: Ten. Behavioural and emotional disorders of childhood. Hyperkinetic and tic disorders.
Organic. Substances. Schizophrenia. Mood. Neurotic. Physiological. Personality. Intellectual. Developmental. Childhood.
On medical wards, delirium is very common. So always think organic first. Save this for your psychiatry posting.
